clusters.state_of_play: Wildfires burning in northwest Ontario and northern Minnesota have stranded a CN Rail freight train and crew, who have since been safely evacuated according to Canadian National. CN Rail has suspended operations in the area. Video footage from near Armstrong, Ontario shows a crew member describing being "encased in flames." Around 838 wildfires are now burning across Canada per the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre, with 112 considered out of control. Ontario smoke pushed Toronto's air quality to worst in the world at times per IQAir, surpassing Kinshasa and New Delhi, with skies turning orange/yellow; Environment Canada has issued formal health warnings and residents are urged to stay indoors. Smoke has drifted into New York City and across the Northeast and Midwest, triggering air quality alerts in at least 16 U.S. states, including a Code Orange alert in the DC region where poor air quality could linger into Friday. A heat dome is driving smoke eastward; roughly 100 million Americans may be affected. Amtrak has added temperature-related speed restrictions on Northeast trains due to extreme heat. Researchers and health officials note that combined exposure to extreme heat and wildfire smoke poses heightened health risks. A northern Minnesota county declared a state of emergency. Separately, a Virginia soccer coach, Ahmed Mohamed, 31, has been charged with scamming athletes out of ~$60K via a fake Italy summer camp.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

Similar grassroots opposition is emerging elsewhere, including Paulding County, Georgia, where furious homeowners packed standing-room-only county commission meetings and held a protest demanding a local moratorium, and in Florida, where residents near a proposed hyperscale data center in Trump's backyard are fuming over water supply risks despite the project's claim of generating over $500 million in annual tax revenue. Opposition to AI data centers is emerging as one of the rare cross-partisan political issues of the cycle. Separately, a PJM power auction covering the nation's largest electrical grid is projected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses across 13 states as a direct result of data center electricity demand. Axios has framed Hochul's moratorium as a replicable Democratic playbook for other governors ahead of the 2026 midterms. The backlash against AI data centers is now global in scope: India is fast-tracking hyperscale data center megaprojects to catch up technologically, but critics warn coastal cities face energy and water depletion with few long-term jobs created. Australia is moving to impose energy and water guardrails on data centers amid the AI boom and also seeks to protect the rights of creators whose work is used to train AI models; Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's Labor government is additionally developing a new national AI framework to address the technology's growing economic and social impacts.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: The UK and EU have signed a post-Brexit Gibraltar treaty at a Brussels ceremony, removing the land border between Gibraltar and Spain and allowing Gibraltar residents to cross using residence cards and Spanish citizens using government ID. The treaty came into effect at midnight, accompanied by a symbolic ceremony and large crowds crossing freely. The old chain-link border fence has been physically torn down, Spanish border checks have been relocated to the international airport and seaport, and Gibraltar is in effect becoming part of the Schengen zone via the EU entry system. Brits entering Gibraltar from Spain will now be fingerprinted under the new arrangements. Tory and Reform MPs are warning this represents a foreign policy 'betrayal' and that Falklands sovereignty could be Labour's next concession. Andy Burnham has secured 349 Labour MP nominations — including all eligible cabinet members — making it impossible for any rival to challenge him, and is confirmed as Britain's next Prime Minister, expected to take office on 20 July. Burnham has pledged a 'broad church' cabinet and party culture, is considering a larger autumn Budget with allies lobbying for a land tax, public control of utilities and expanded devolution. A new Real Rates Reform Alliance is now also pressing him to go further on business rates reform, calling for a 2% online sales tax to fund a 37% cut in rates for physical retailers. He plans to scrap David Lammy's jury-trial abolition proposals. He voted to back immigration curbs at the Immigration and Asylum Bill's second reading despite a threatened left-wing revolt. Burnham has not uttered a word in the Commons chamber since being sworn in as Makerfield MP on 22 June. Tories are demanding Parliament delay its summer recess to scrutinise him before he takes office. The Reform UK/Farage financial scrutiny story continues: the £5m crypto donor is now linked to Tether, a giant and secretive cryptocurrency firm that Farage has publicly championed. Separately, Farage refused taxpayer-funded security as inadequate, with Reform UK continuing to fund his personal protection.

Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: Missouri has declared a state of emergency in response to severe storms and flash flooding described as once-in-a-millennium rainfall; Governor Mike Kehoe activated the state emergency operations center. At least one person has died — identified as Faith Gregory of Crawford County, whose home was swept from its foundation and whose body was found by volunteers late Saturday. More than 202 children and staff were airlifted by Missouri National Guard Black Hawk helicopters from Camp Taum Sauk in Lesterville after nearby roads were washed away. Around 20 people who climbed to the roof of a collapsed building at the Barecat Getaway campground in Reynolds County were also airlifted to safety. Some campers climbed into trees to escape rising waters, prompting a state mutual aid request. Up to a foot of rain fell overnight in southeastern Missouri, prompting more than 350 rescues from floodwaters overall. More than 20 million people across at least 14 states from Colorado to Pennsylvania are under flood watches through Saturday. The flash-flood threat is continuing into Sunday, extending from Tennessee to West Virginia. The threat has expanded significantly in Texas: a state of emergency has been declared covering nearly 60 counties, a flash flood emergency has been triggered in Central Texas, more than a foot of rain has fallen in parts of Texas in 24 hours leading to dozens of rescues, highways have been washed out, and motorists have been stranded. A tornado was spawned in San Antonio. Kerr County officials — site of last year's Camp Mystic disaster that killed 28 people — are in contact with summer camps now at risk. Forecasters warn of isolated totals of up to 15 inches possible. Camp Mystic operators have moved five lawsuits filed by families over last year's catastrophic flooding to federal court, citing bankruptcy. A heat dome is simultaneously driving triple-digit temperatures from Southern California to the Northeast, threatening record-breaking heat. Separately, days of torrential monsoon rain have triggered major flooding in Bangladesh, killing at least 51 people and leaving millions stranded in the south-east of the country, with food supply shortages reported. On the immigration enforcement front: a Venezuelan man (Jesús Manuel Arenas-Silva, 45) died in ICE custody in Georgia, becoming the 22nd such death this year. A 28-year-old man fleeing ICE agents in St. Augustine, Florida was struck and killed by a tractor-trailer, the third death in a week involving ICE encounters following fatal shootings of two men during vehicle stops in Maine and Texas six days apart. In response, ICE has suspended most vehicle stops. Mexico has now launched legal action in the US over the deaths of 17 Mexican nationals in ICE custody or during enforcement operations, with the foreign ministry filing criminal complaints with US state prosecutors. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, who had pledged to escalate Mexico's response, also rejected remarks by DEA head Terry Cole linking Mexico's government to cartels, calling them a baseless political statement.

Iran claims to have destroyed the US Fifth Fleet command centre and targeted a US naval support base in Bahrain's capital, with sirens reported in Manama. Dubai has announced plans to build a new port to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf states more broadly are exploring alternative routes. Former officials say a stable peace appears elusive and characterise the current Hormuz campaign as Trump's third major strategic shift in the Iran conflict. Separately, Ukraine has struck more than 100 Russian vessels in the Sea of Azov over nine days and has also struck 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Trump has said Putin is ready to make a deal to end the Ukraine war, though Russia has warned that Western troops enforcing any ceasefire would be treated as military targets. The EU and Ukraine have signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures, combining Ukraine's battlefield expertise with EU scale. Treasury Secretary Bessent has announced a Trump gold coin featuring the sitting president will go into production. clusters.state_of_play: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed an executive order imposing the first statewide moratorium on new large (hyperscaler) data centers for one year, citing energy grid, environmental, and ratepayer cost concerns, including ensuring New Yorkers do not bear costs of transmission and infrastructure build-outs, while state lawmakers draft a nation-leading regulatory framework. The moratorium is drawing backlash from critics who say it will further damage upstate New York's already sagging economy. President Trump has publicly blasted the moratorium, demanding Hochul reverse the policy immediately. The action follows a growing left-wing grassroots campaign, backed by Sanders-aligned progressives, opposing AI data center expansion. Similar grassroots opposition is emerging elsewhere, including Paulding County, Georgia, where furious homeowners packed standing-room-only county commission meetings and held a protest demanding a local moratorium, and in Florida, where residents near a proposed hyperscale data center in Trump's backyard are fuming over water supply risks despite the project's claim of generating over $500 million in annual tax revenue. Opposition to AI data centers is emerging as one of the rare cross-partisan political issues of the cycle. Separately, a PJM power auction covering the nation's largest electrical grid is projected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses across 13 states as a direct result of data center electricity demand. Axios has framed Hochul's moratorium as a replicable Democratic playbook for other governors ahead of the 2026 midterms. The backlash against AI data centers is now global in scope: India is fast-tracking hyperscale data center megaprojects to catch up technologically, but critics warn coastal cities face energy and water depletion with few long-term jobs created. Australia is moving to impose energy and water guardrails on data centers amid the AI boom and also seeks to protect the rights of creators whose work is used to train AI models; Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's Labor government is additionally developing a new national AI framework to address the technology's growing economic and social impacts.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.title: NY enacts data center moratorium

items.title: NY enacts data center moratorium

ledger.unique: Frames moratorium as signal of growing mainstream political pushback to AI growth.

clusters.state_of_play: New York Governor Kathy Hochul has signed an executive order imposing the first statewide moratorium on new large (hyperscaler) data centers for one year, citing energy grid, environmental, and ratepayer cost concerns, including ensuring New Yorkers do not bear costs of transmission and infrastructure build-outs, while state lawmakers draft a nation-leading regulatory framework. The moratorium is drawing backlash from critics who say it will further damage upstate New York's already sagging economy. President Trump has publicly blasted the moratorium, demanding Hochul reverse the policy immediately. The action follows a growing left-wing grassroots campaign, backed by Sanders-aligned progressives, opposing AI data center expansion. Similar grassroots opposition is emerging elsewhere, including Paulding County, Georgia, where furious homeowners packed standing-room-only county commission meetings and held a protest demanding a local moratorium, and in Florida, where residents near a proposed hyperscale data center in Trump's backyard are fuming over water supply risks despite the project's claim of generating over $500 million in annual tax revenue. Opposition to AI data centers is emerging as one of the rare cross-partisan political issues of the cycle. Separately, a PJM power auction covering the nation's largest electrical grid is projected to add $6.3 billion in additional charges to consumers and businesses across 13 states as a direct result of data center electricity demand. Axios has framed Hochul's moratorium as a replicable Democratic playbook for other governors ahead of the 2026 midterms. The backlash against AI data centers is now global in scope: India is fast-tracking hyperscale data center megaprojects to catch up technologically, but critics warn coastal cities face energy and water depletion with few long-term jobs created. Australia is moving to impose energy and water guardrails on data centers amid the AI boom and also seeks to protect the rights of creators whose work is used to train AI models; Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's Labor government is additionally developing a new national AI framework to address the technology's growing economic and social impacts.

clusters.state_of_play: The US has launched fresh waves of strikes on Iran including daytime strikes, and has reimposed a naval blockade on all Iranian ports. US strikes have hit port cities of Bushehr and Bandar Abbas, as well as a 90-minute attack on Iran's Greater Tunb Island targeting cruise missile storage and launch sites. US attacks have killed dozens in Iran, pushing a fragile ceasefire closer to collapse. A Situation Room meeting was held to plan a wider offensive broader in scope than the current Strait of Hormuz campaign. Trump warned strikes would intensify next week if Iran does not cooperate in peace talks, while also calling off a previously announced 20% fee on Hormuz shipping, replacing it with investment and trade deals with Gulf Arab states. US strikes hit an Iranian army barracks, killing at least 7 troops and wounding more than 260 people across the country. Iran has threatened to halt all Middle East energy exports in response to the blockade. Iran claims to have destroyed the US Fifth Fleet command centre and targeted a US naval support base in Bahrain's capital, with sirens reported in Manama. Iran has also attacked Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan; Jordan shot down three Iranian missiles. Iran claims to have killed 3 US service members in Kuwait, while the official US death toll stands at 14. The US used sea drones in combat for the first time to strike an Iranian submarine and ship maintenance facility near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude is above $87 per barrel. Dubai has announced plans to build a new port to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf states more broadly are exploring alternative routes. Former officials say a stable peace appears elusive and characterise the current Hormuz campaign as Trump's third major strategic shift in the Iran conflict. Separately, Ukraine has struck more than 100 Russian vessels in the Sea of Azov over nine days and has also struck 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Russia's Agriculture Ministry is actively seeking alternative shipping routes and denies the strikes will affect export capacity, though Russian oil at sea is near a year-high as Moscow struggles to sell its exports. Russian strikes on Odesa killed at least 3 people and wounded 3 others. Trump has said Putin is ready to make a deal to end the Ukraine war, though Russia has warned that Western troops enforcing any ceasefire would be treated as military targets. The EU and Ukraine have signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures, combining Ukraine's battlefield expertise with EU scale. Treasury Secretary Bessent has announced a Trump gold coin featuring the sitting president will go into production. In China, official data shows GDP grew 4.3% in Q2, the weakest quarterly growth since late 2022, driven by slow consumer demand despite a surge in exports. DeepSeek is weighing an IPO and considering raising new private funds after completing a first financing round that valued the company at $52 billion; Zhipu has separately embraced an AGI positioning. Hong Kong police raided two bookstores and arrested five people for allegedly selling seditious publications, underscoring the political changes that have eroded the territory's once-open publishing environment.

Five people have been arrested on suspicion of deliberately starting the fires, including a volunteer firefighter who admitted to setting fire to twigs using matches and gasoline; a second suspect admitted to accidentally starting a fire by discarding a cigarette. Officials described the blaze as of 'exceptional scale', with road and rail links disrupted. clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: Wildfires burning in northwest Ontario and northern Minnesota have stranded a CN Rail freight train and crew, who have since been safely evacuated according to Canadian National. CN Rail has suspended operations in the area. Video footage from near Armstrong, Ontario shows a crew member describing being "encased in flames." Around 838 wildfires are now burning across Canada per the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre, with 112 considered out of control. Ontario smoke pushed Toronto's air quality to worst in the world at times per IQAir, surpassing Kinshasa and New Delhi, with skies turning orange/yellow; Environment Canada has issued formal health warnings and residents are urged to stay indoors. Smoke has drifted into New York City and across the Northeast and Midwest, triggering air quality alerts in at least 16 U.S. states, including a Code Orange alert in the DC region where poor air quality could linger into Friday. A heat dome is driving smoke eastward; roughly 100 million Americans may be affected. Amtrak has added temperature-related speed restrictions on Northeast trains due to extreme heat. Researchers and health officials note that combined exposure to extreme heat and wildfire smoke poses heightened health risks. A northern Minnesota county declared a state of emergency. Separately, a Virginia soccer coach, Ahmed Mohamed, 31, has been charged with scamming athletes out of ~$60K via a fake Italy summer camp.

clusters.state_of_play: The US has launched fresh waves of strikes on Iran including daytime strikes, and has reimposed a naval blockade on all Iranian ports. US strikes have hit port cities of Bushehr and Bandar Abbas, as well as a 90-minute attack on Iran's Greater Tunb Island targeting cruise missile storage and launch sites. US attacks have killed dozens in Iran, pushing a fragile ceasefire closer to collapse. A Situation Room meeting was held to plan a wider offensive broader in scope than the current Strait of Hormuz campaign. Trump warned strikes would intensify next week if Iran does not cooperate in peace talks, while also calling off a previously announced 20% fee on Hormuz shipping, replacing it with investment and trade deals with Gulf Arab states. US strikes hit an Iranian army barracks, killing at least 7 troops and wounding more than 260 people across the country. Iran has threatened to halt all Middle East energy exports in response to the blockade. Iran claims to have destroyed the US Fifth Fleet command centre and targeted a US naval support base in Bahrain's capital, with sirens reported in Manama. Iran has also attacked Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan; Jordan shot down three Iranian missiles. Iran claims to have killed 3 US service members in Kuwait, while the official US death toll stands at 14. The US used sea drones in combat for the first time to strike an Iranian submarine and ship maintenance facility near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude is above $87 per barrel. Dubai has announced plans to build a new port to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, and Gulf states more broadly are exploring alternative routes. Former officials say a stable peace appears elusive and characterise the current Hormuz campaign as Trump's third major strategic shift in the Iran conflict. Separately, Ukraine has struck more than 100 Russian vessels in the Sea of Azov over nine days and has also struck 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Russia's Agriculture Ministry is actively seeking alternative shipping routes and denies the strikes will affect export capacity, though Russian oil at sea is near a year-high as Moscow struggles to sell its exports. Russian strikes on Odesa killed at least 3 people and wounded 3 others. Trump has said Putin is ready to make a deal to end the Ukraine war, though Russia has warned that Western troops enforcing any ceasefire would be treated as military targets. The EU and Ukraine have signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures, combining Ukraine's battlefield expertise with EU scale. Treasury Secretary Bessent has announced a Trump gold coin featuring the sitting president will go into production. In China, official data shows GDP grew 4.3% in Q2, the weakest quarterly growth since late 2022, driven by slow consumer demand despite a surge in exports. DeepSeek is weighing an IPO and considering raising new private funds after completing a first financing round that valued the company at $52 billion; Zhipu has separately embraced an AGI positioning. Hong Kong police raided two bookstores and arrested five people for allegedly selling seditious publications, underscoring the political changes that have eroded the territory's once-open publishing environment.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC) died Saturday at age 71 from a heart attack. President Trump publicly recommended that South Carolina Gov. Henry McMaster appoint Graham's sister, Darline Graham Nordone, calling it a 'fabulous tribute,' and Sen. Tim Scott is also pushing for her appointment. Darline spoke briefly with the New York Post about the loss of her brother. McMaster is expected to announce his pick at a press conference. A White House plan is reportedly in place to avoid appointing Rep. Nancy Mace, and at least one Fox News figure has withdrawn from contention. Republicans in South Carolina have begun jockeying for the full six-year Senate seat election separate from the caretaker appointment. Ukraine is grappling with the loss of a key Trump-orbit ally. Social media has seen false claims of criminal action in Graham's death, a California nurse who pre-death wished harm on Graham and Trump, and comedian Margaret Cho's viral video mocking Graham's death. South Carolina lawmakers including Tim Scott, Nancy Mace, William Timmons, and Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette paid tribute. On The View, Sunny Hostin said Graham 'betrayed his country for power' while Ana Navarro condemned those celebrating his death. Graham had become Darline's legal guardian after their parents died 15 months apart and called her the closest person in his life.

clusters.state_of_play: IBM issued a preliminary Q2 earnings warning, blaming a client spending shift away from software and infrastructure toward hardware (servers and storage), driven partly by AI investment. CEO Arvind Krishna told CNBC that some major deals were put on hold toward the end of the quarter as businesses rethink spending. Shares fell ~25% Tuesday, wiping out ~$70 billion in market value — a steeper single-day drop than IBM suffered during the 1987 Black Monday crash. The selloff spread to the broader software sector, including Microsoft. Cybersecurity stocks rallied on Krishna's AI spending comments.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: The US cyclosporiasis outbreak continues to worsen, with cases now reported across 40 states and more than 5,500 confirmed; CDC's tally of confirmed or under-investigation cases stands at nearly 7,000, with 1,645 lab-confirmed. Michigan alone now accounts for 3,300+ cases, with officials pointing to lettuce or salad greens as a likely source. CDC has identified a link among four Midwestern states and expects the outbreaks to continue through August. Taco Bell has pulled implicated ingredients. RFK Jr. faces scrutiny over CDC's response, and cyclospora was dropped from the federal monitoring program last summer. Funding cuts are also hampering CDC's ability to track the outbreak, with no source yet confirmed. On Wednesday, Trump's CDC director nominee Erica Schwartz faced Senate confirmation, vowing to 'never betray the science' and pledge 'radical transparency,' but struggled to convince senators she would stand up to RFK Jr. Separately, Trump's health emergency preparedness nominee Sean Kaufman walked back past comments skeptical of Covid-19 and hepatitis B vaccine safety, drawing a heated exchange with Sen. Cassidy. Separately, a new Legionnaires' disease outbreak has emerged on Manhattan's Upper East Side with 60 cases; the source remains unclear. The DRC Ebola outbreak — now the fastest-growing in history, killing roughly 100 per week — continues to worsen. Confirmed cases have reached 2,011 with 754 deaths; WHO warns the true count may be 2–4 times larger. Critically, 80% of new cases are now emerging from unknown transmission chains, meaning the outbreak is spreading faster than it can be tracked. The outbreak has spread to additional DRC provinces. Maternal mortality has doubled in the outbreak zone, with an estimated 63,000 pregnant women at risk as mothers avoid hospitals. WHO has launched the first clinical trial of an antiviral drug to prevent Bundibugyo strain Ebola infection, and Oxford University has begun human trials of a new Ebola vaccine in the UK. Healthcare workers at a DRC Ebola treatment centre remain on strike over unpaid salaries, and health workers in Ituri province have separately begun striking over unpaid wages. A second US national has been evacuated to Germany for treatment, and the Trump administration is barring Americans in the DRC from returning to the US on commercial flights. CDC travel restrictions have been extended to also cover some travelers from Uganda and South Sudan. The Ebola outbreak also threatens to cancel a UK-backed kidney transplant programme in Uganda. Separately, UK health officials are warning of a rapid rise in imported Zika virus cases, and Los Angeles County has reported its first West Nile virus case of 2026.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

At the peak of the June heatwave, an estimated 440 people per day died over its three-day peak. Researchers warn the worst is yet to come. Separately, the heatwave also boosted UK retail spending in June, with total retail sales up 1.9% year on year and online sales up 5.1%.

clusters.state_of_play: Russia has suspended shipping in the Sea of Azov after Ukraine targeted 90 vessels, including shadow fleet oil tankers, in under a week. Ukraine also released video of strikes on 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea, including 17 oil tankers. Ukraine's drone forces chief Robert Brovdi confirmed overnight strikes on 10 tankers, 4 ferries, and Russia's Syzran refinery in the Samara region. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.

clusters.state_of_play: The Trump administration, fulfilling a prior pledge, directed the National Park Service to replace panels at the President's House slavery memorial in Philadelphia overnight. The new exhibit drew criticism from advocates and Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle L. Parker, who said the removal happened under cover of darkness. Critics argue the new panels present a sanitized view of US history. Separately, a $69 million NPS exhibit beneath the Lincoln Memorial, opened less than a month ago, is reported to be endangering rare 1860s copies of the Emancipation Proclamation and Thirteenth Amendment due to defective light screens and unsafe temperatures, according to NPS staff. In an unrelated Philadelphia incident, Vietnam veteran George Barr, 75, has been charged with the murder of Silas Hanrahan, 21, a British illegal immigrant and alleged member of a traveler conman gang, who was shot dead at Barr's home; neighbors have made disturbing allegations about Hanrahan's conduct prior to the shooting. Also unrelated: a British pub landlady, 65, was shot dead in front of her husband during a Caribbean holiday. The attacks have triggered a nationwide fuel shortage in Russia, with queues reported at fuel stations and Russia now seeking gasoline imports from India in a reversal of trade flow. These strikes fall under a formal 40-day campaign Zelenskyy announced on 26 June, ordering Ukraine's state security service to target Russian territory to compel an end to the war. Russia has struck back: a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv and further strikes across Ukraine have killed at least 16 people over two days. Mayor Vitali Klitschko previously reported emergency services battling fires across the capital following an earlier missile strike. Ukraine is also targeting Crimea as part of a strategy to demonstrate Putin's failure to defend the peninsula. On POW executions, a Ukrainian intelligence official told AFP that more than 900 military personnel have been killed in more than 340 incidents since 2022. The UN reported June was the deadliest month for Ukrainian civilians since April 2022, with 293 killed and 1,990 wounded, bringing total verified civilian deaths to 16,431 since February 2022. Inside Ukraine, President Zelenskyy's dismissal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov has triggered rare wartime protests across the country, with thousands of soldiers, veterans, and civilians demanding his reappointment; the deputy air force commander has also resigned in protest. Parliament has now approved Koretskyi as the new Prime Minister, following PM Yulia Svyrydenko's resignation. The EU and Ukraine signed a drone deal to boost joint production and establish joint ventures; Brussels has also allowed Kyiv to use part of a €6bn EU tranche to buy Chinese drone parts that are in short supply in Europe. The EU separately failed to agree its latest round of sanctions against Russia. UK PM Keir Starmer travelled to Kyiv to meet Zelenskyy, reaffirming UK support, in what is described as a farewell trip before he hands over to Andy Burnham. On the Coalition of the Willing, Bulgaria's PM Rumen Radev has withdrawn Bulgaria from the group, and Ukrainian politician Kira Rudik has warned that upcoming European national elections could produce a very different coalition next year. Separately, Poland-Ukraine relations face strain over Kyiv's decision to honour WWII fighters responsible for killing roughly 100,000 Poles.
